name: Name
title: Emergence Part 4
body: By Erik Reiersen

name: Name
body: Part I It began with Rhyas’ grief, holding the last remaining vestige of her sister Saeryn: her athanc. The rest of Saeryn had been obliterated as she tried to pass through the Henge Hold gate to provoke the goddess Cyriss in an effort to trap some of her power, only to be destroyed by the Goddess beyond. But now Rhyas would have to pay the dragon they fled, Everblight, for both of their mistakes. Yet as she took her sister’s athanc shard and embedded it in her chest next to her own, she found Saeryn was still close at hand, trapped within the shard itself.  Flee this place, Saeryn warned her through the shard. We’re hunted even now... Find somewhere remote and hidden... Our destiny is to lead, but not the Nyss... Both driven from the battlefield at Henge Hold and lured by a faraway song in the Wyrmwall Mountains, Rhyas absconded, ultimately descending underground to find what she was drawn to, a cephalyx hive, one vulnerable enough for her to decimate. And from their remains, both mechanical and flesh, she used the power she shared with Saeryn to create new beings, ones the world had never seen before: the Khymaera.

name: Name
body: From deeper within the caverns, the hive’s leader, Exulon Nixian, watched and puzzled over Rhyas, especially as the Nyss infused some of her own power in the first hellish creature she created. So alluring were Rhyas’ capabilities that Exulon Nixian decided she must possess the Nyss and set plans in motion to capture Rhyas. And at Henge Hold, among the myriad dead and dying, two of the dragon Everblight’s warlocks, Fyanna and Lylyth, searched for the two renegade Nyss sisters and their athanc shards, which Everblight claimed as his own. Not finding the surviving Rhyas, the warlocks gathered their dragonspawn forces and turned their search toward the Wyrmwall Mountains in the distance… Part 2 For six months, Rhyas’ draconic horror, Rassyk, learned the art of war and an understanding of the new world he lived in, his education drawn from the memories of both Rhyas and Saeryn contained within their athanc shards. He also sensed the approaching forces of Everblight and the constriction around the newly created Khymaera as the cephalyx closed in.

name: Name
body: As one of Exulon Nixian’s own, the silexus named Yortho, plotted against her—as did another silexus, Nostilla, watching and waiting for Yortho’s failure in order to personally benefit from his downfall. Exulon Nixian made good on her goal to bring Rhyas to imprisonment: she sent Yortho with a large strike force to capture the Nyss, but Rhyas was not so easily taken. Rhyas allowed a metamorphosis to overcome her, turning her to more monstrous draconic beast than Nyss, and giving her the power she needed to obliterate Yortho and his forces with Rassyk’s aid. Undeterred, Exulon Nixian began to lay the foundation for her next plan of attack. Elsewhere, the forces of Everblight, led by the warlocks Fyanna and Lylyth, zeroed in on the underground caverns where Rhyas had been hidden for all these months. They came at the behest of the dragon Everblight, but they bore with them concerns: another dragon, Blighterghast, waited in the mountain range. But their goal remained to find Rhyas and recover the two shards she still carried and used.

name: Name
body: Over the coming weeks, as her power waxed and waned, Rhyas—with aid from Saeryn’s presence inside her athanc shard—created her next warlock monstrosity, another akin to Rassyk. This one, Shyryss, was designed to be a scout, a stealth agent, one with more freedom of thought than Rassyk, one that would be useful as she sensed Everblight’s agents closing in. She also designed Hydrixes and more Vypexes, warbeasts to best the enemy, and even more servants for the newfound Khymaera forces. She hid them in ambush, in preparation for the arrival of Fyanna and Lylyth, and when those forces of Everblight came close enough, she had them attack. But the forces directed by Nixian had waited for this moment as well. They attacked the Khymaera just as the Khymaera attacked the Legion of Everblight forces, and Rhyas found herself trapped in the middle. Desperate for victory, she assumed her dragon-like form once more, but before she could overwhelm the two Everblight warlocks, Nixian’s forces—undead Cryxian mechanithralls and other undead hosts—overwhelmed them all, driving one of the warlocks away and leaving Rhyas to deal with Nixian herself in a brutal negotiation that resulted in a commitment from Rhyas to use her powers to build Nixian anew in exchange for Nixian’s gift of an entire army to aid Rhyas’ goals for the Khymaera. Taking the athanc from the fallen of the two warlocks, Rhyas agreed to the deal.

name: Name
body: Even as this brokering took place, a Cygnaran force led by the warcaster Sergeant Lucia Castillo, seven months into pursuing what they thought were grave robbers who had looted and destroyed at Henge Hold, came across evidence of the passage of a powerful and horrific force. Terrified by what she had discovered, Castillo led her soldiers on a race to report to the nearest outpost before they came upon the enemy. But they were detected as they fled… Part 3 Shyryss, the stealth agent Rhyas created as another powerhouse for the new Khymaera, was finally put to use: she was sent out of the caverns to the surface, where, after a nasty encounter with entombed undead of unknown origins, she finally reached the approaching enemy forces of the dragon Blighterghast. Everblight’s forces come, she warned their emissary, and he can only be defeated with knowledge we possess. She then delivered Rhyas’ message regarding Everblight’s vulnerability and how the Khymaera could use it to Blighterghast’s advantage: if they defeated Everblight in the North, his last remaining athanc shard, hosted by a warlock currently beyond reach, could be destroyed and the dragon killed—and Rhyas’ growing faction could lead Blighterghast’s army to that warlock.

name: Name
body: The forces of Blighterghast and those of the Khymaera reached an accord.

name: Name
body:
Lieutenant Fowler studied an ordered pile of reports while his communications liaison Parker, who acted mostly as his secretary, fidgeted. Fowler’s office was stark and efficient, much like his own features. Small wire-rimmed glasses sat forward on his beak-like nose, which defined his gaunt hairless head. He was old for a lieutenant, a product of the frantic restructuring as the military rebuilt itself. His office was sparse nearly to the point of being barren, containing only two simple wooden chairs, an otherwise clean desk save for his current paperwork, and a Cygnus with the 4th Army designation adorning the wall behind him. He seemed completely indifferent to being told that the scouting party hunting the so-called Reapers of Henge Hold had returned with urgent news. Parker was about to nervously repeat the announcement when he was silenced by Fowler’s single raised finger. After several minutes, the lieutenant finally broke the silence. "Send her in, please."
Parker let out his breath, opened the door, and said softly, "The lieutenant will see you now."

name: Name
body: Sergeant Castillo quickly stumbled into the room, fighting exhaustion and still gasping for breath as she made her way to the chair. She knew she must stay conscious at least long enough to deliver her message. Her uniform was tattered and stained with a mixture of mud and blood. She had multiple visible wounds and was missing a good portion of her left ear, leaving her neck and one shoulder stained red. All manner of foliage was stuck in her uniform; her hair was matted from a three-day death race through the forest from their pursuers. Ultimately, she survived long enough to reach a base where she could report. She struggled to speak. "Lieutenant, a massive force—" She could barely stop herself from continuing as Fowler snapped without looking up from his paperwork. "Are we no longer saluting, Sergeant?" She choked but instinctively shot to attention, saluting as a wave of nausea flowed over her. She had tried to reach a watch post to simply wire in her report, but the post she had made it to was doomed before the message could be sent. Her pursuers were too close on her tail and had overwhelmed the unprepared garrison. With the local HQ so close and better defended, she redirected herself there, still only a step ahead. She knew Fowler to be a pedantic and pitiless man, but as the one who had sent her off in the first place, he would be receptive to her findings, she had assumed. But maybe not.

name: Name
body: Castillo began to ask for permission to continue when she was cut off once more. Fowler looked up from his paperwork and regarded her with unconcealed displeasure. His eyes traced slowly up and down as he assessed her appearance. "Not all of us have completely abandoned our sense of pride and decorum," he said as he returned her salute. "Permission to be seated, sir." Castillo strained with evident pain as Fowler steepled his fingers as if in consideration, then offered an exaggerated gesture to the chair before returning his hands to an A-frame. The sergeant let out a deep sigh as she settled. She realized she was uncertain if she’d be able to get back up, but that didn’t matter at this moment. She began again, fighting to stay awake. "Sir, my apologies, we’ve been double-timing for three days and harried the whole way, but I must report what we saw. There is a massive force of blighted creatures moving toward our cities from the Wyrmwalls. We must immediately muster everything we can—"

name: Name
body: Fowler held up his hand to stop her. He sucked on his teeth, caving in his already sunken cheeks, then offered his response with a dismissive sigh as he removed his glasses and rubbed his nose where they had rested. "Yes, sergeant, three days. Three days to deliver this urgent message, but you couldn’t find three minutes to make yourself presentable? I am told only two of you returned. Care to explain where the rest of the unit I put you in charge of is at this time?" Castillo swallowed. "I…I don’t know why you are being like this. They’re dead. We’ve been tracking killers for months and found they were scouts for an army that marches upon Cygnar as we speak. Sir." She turned to Parker, but he avoided eye contact and did his best to seem invisible. Fowler, unfazed, clapped back. "Oh, I’m quite aware of your exploits, Sergeant. I’ve read every report and I’ve seen the resources your team has demanded." He tapped the stack of logistics reports. "You have fruitlessly holidayed in the wilderness for the better part of a year, and now you intend to tell me that these scouts you were supposed to be tracking took out a handful of sentries over a graveyard in the middle of our nation then wandered all around the mountains for half a year eluding your team as their master plan of an attack on Cygnar? Not only that, but hidden right before you was a full invasion force that crossed our borders unseen and also somehow managed to elude our scouts?"

name: Name
body: He eyed her as if awaiting a response, but she didn’t bother. He said, "The only reason I have suffered your unit’s prolonged failure is that without a scapegoat for the attack, we needed to keep hope alive amongst the disenfranchised masses and offer the impression that we were seeking justice. "I had hoped that in time, out of desperation to save some face, you might show up with the body of a wolf or an unfortunate woodsman so we could close the book on this embarrassment. Instead, you managed to manifest a bigger problem for us, and now you spew nonsense to save that face when confronted by your failings." Fowler leaned back and slid down in his chair. He sighed and seemed to be speaking to himself. "The Infernal War nearly broke this country, you know. Not a single citizen went unaffected or a single life untouched. Things looked as if they could be rectified, but when we began the recovery, we failed to see a much more insidious threat the infernals left behind. A sickness that didn’t threaten merely the population but the very culture and identity of Cygnar itself. Fear. Just as nearly universal peace was enacted and hope of moving forward appeared, a new unidentified danger presented itself, striking our soldiers at Henge Hold and vanishing into the night as an ongoing looming menace to stability."

name: Name
body: He sat up straight in his chair again while making eye contact with Castillo. His tone darkened. "I, in my most optimistic foolishness, selected a green but eager sergeant as my agent to resolve it quickly, but I failed to see the possible ramifications or how many would suffer as a result of my decision. Your ineffectiveness has reflected directly upon me. "People were hopeful and eager for resolution, but time waxed on. Crops went unharvested, ore unmined, and goods untraded. The public didn’t leave their homes as they held tight to what little they had and wouldn’t dare to risk. Hopeful eyes desperately sought news of safety every day. News of our success in ending this threat! "But shortages created by the war were exacerbated. As they spread, desperation began to set in. Citizen turned against citizen, good people stabbed in the street for the likes of pocket change or a loaf of bread. Every day, the quality of life degraded in my sector as common folk were pushed to the edge… Oh, but not for you… No, according to these reports, you were quite well supplied while they suffered."

name: Name
body: Castillo sat speechless. Fowler sighed and squinted as he set his glasses on the desk and rubbed his eyes. "Do you know why Captain Kessler reassigned me from logistical analysis? My attention to detail and understanding of the greater needs of the army as a whole, but most importantly, to shield him from anything that could mar his reputation." Castillo couldn’t help but think it was due to the dearth of leadership after so many of the valiant fell in the Infernal War, but she refrained from sharing her thoughts aloud. Fowler continued. "Under ordinary circumstances, this might mark the end of your career, but… in this case, there is an alternative…" His voice softened. "Before your arrival, we received word from a watch post that there were signs of a larger than usual migration venturing down from the mountains, presumably Tharn, but unseasonable weather was making it difficult to spot them. Likely the same group you and your team fumbled into and misidentified in your inexperienced panic. We are mobilizing the 4th to intercept them with overwhelming force. Captain Kessler shall lead as we wipe them out, label them the culprits, and put a pretty little bow on this whole ordeal. Once word gets out, you will look quite the fool for running around the mountains ineffectually for months as well as losing your team, but… you could instead be the hero who warned us just in time before an attack that threatened Cygnar.

name: Name
body: "Now, your career trajectory is entirely dependent upon your next decisions. All you must do is swallow your pride and keep any of your blighted nonsense to yourself. It’s truly the best-case scenario for you." Castillo shook her head. "We know the attackers weren’t Tharn. We fought them. Their blood is dried in my clothes! There was a witness—" The lieutenant stopped her. "It’s been taken care of. It matters not at all at this point who or what killed the guards. There are countless beasts of wanton impulse that blanket these lands, and we have no credible leads on any of them that could put an end to this. Whatever it was is long gone, and our security has tightened in response. What we need now, what Cygnar needs, is for all parties to play their part and put this humiliation to rest. The witness understands that his memory may have been a bit hazy about that night, and he also understands that the people need a win." He put his glasses back on, folded his hands, and donned a condescending smile. In a biting tone, he said, "And how about you, Sergeant? Are you able to put the nation above your selfish need to be right?"

name: Name
body: *** Lylyth had fled too far and fast to pursue. After Fyanna was slain, Rhyas attempted to track down her accomplice, but the effort was in vain. The scattered stars of athancs that Rhyas had sensed encircling their home from other approaching warlocks had consolidated into a dense constellation as they now respected the hazard before them and readied for the known threat they faced. They knew where she was, but they had yet to meet her children. The cephalyx hive was thoroughly stripped of materials that were gathered into Nixian’s cathedral, which now functioned as a larder flush with the exulon’s chemically lobotomized horde. Nixian revealed the hidden maps of the hive as promised, concealed behind puzzled walls only operable with telekinesis. At first, Rhyas was confused by the scale—until she realized that it wasn’t a local map but a map of Immoren itself. Manifold spiderwebs of corridors interlaced with a noticeable drought of networks in the vicinity of Rhul. Silexus Nostilla was not present when they came to gather the motionless army for preparation. She was more capable than Nixian had realized: she had circumvented her immobilizing implants and escaped. She would likely run to a neighboring hive, but they would be cautious in response, even if they chose to act upon her rantings. Rhyas needed to bolster their own army immediately if they were to fight what amounted to nearly the entire Legion of Everblight. After consuming Fyanna’s shard, Rhyas would have enough power to fulfill the promise to Nixian. While Saeryn encouraged full betrayal, Rhyas saw too much value in the ancient mind to fully waste it and felt Nixian was too careful to not have additional failsafe protocols in place to, at a minimum, justify a charade.

name: Name
body: In the safety of the cathedral, Rhyas pressed the athanc into her chest. When Fyanna’s shard touched Rhyas’, a flash of rage exploded from it as Everblight’s presence was violently erased. As Rhyas had hoped, pure intimations of Fyanna, uncorrupted by Everblight’s will, remained evident although scarce. Fyanna might be no more, but her existence would live on, conglomerated into the being Saeryn and Rhyas had become. The absorption was smooth and uncontested as the Cyriss energies evicted any opposition. Only the dormant memory of the previous vessel remained. Nixian had prepared a pile of the finest metals stolen or discovered over a century of pillaging and was afire with anticipation as Rhyas raised her hand and began the process. Nixian’s withered remains, encased within her armored chamber, boiled and separated as the metal egg dissolved around her. She delighted in the pain; it symbolized metamorphosis. The torment increased as she was driven beyond any tolerable agony while she artificially kept herself aware with nerve-stimulating implants. She could have disabled her own nerve centers but left them to accentuate the moment of her divine transmutation. When the procedure reached her mind, a new untold pain racked her.

name: Name
body: As she felt herself start to slip away, fear gripped her for the first time in decades. Treachery at this point in the process left Nixian helpless to her fate. Rhyas agreed with Saeryn’s stance that they couldn’t risk their plans being jeopardized by the alien whims of an ancient cephalyx in their midst. Thus, Rhyas imprinted Nixian’s consciousness onto her own athanc and attempted to excise all but that which proved academic or informative. Once complete, she finished obliterating all that remained of Nixian as she was reconfigured into her new guise. As a form of insurance, her contemporary form was intentionally frail and lacked martial predisposition in case any of the cephalyx’s backstabbing ways somehow survived the transfiguration. Rhyas implanted all Nixian’s knowledge of the hive, locations of traps, understanding of rivals, and sorcerous talents into this new arrangement. Nyxyan was offered to her as a name by Rhyas which she in turn chose, to honor the memory of the being that provided the matter and arcane persuasion she was woven from while using the spelling and pronunciation to honor her bequeathed Nyss heritage. Rhyas had rendered Nixian’s soul down to its base components, destroying everything else as she used this energy to power the recomposition. Saeryn believed it was a mistake to leave any trace of the cephalyx, but Rhyas saw value in retaining some of the ancient and experienced flesh crafter’s mind.

name: Name
body: In the scant days that passed afterward, it became clear that Nyxyan perfectly embodied their needs. She was a sinewy and lithe serpentine humanoid with four graceful arms to assist with the motions required for flesh spinning and spellcasting. Rhyas filled Nyxyan with the memories of her harsh tutelage in sorcery as well as the rituals and power of those fought alongside and against. Rhyas then focused Nyxyan’s training on assisting with the effort to reform the cephalyx horde into a colony of warriors and beasts prepared for the inevitable war with her former slaver. Nyxyan was gifted with extreme arcane prowess that could assist with the shaping of their spawn, yet she bore the mind of a hunter and proceeded to use her time to evolve her shadowmancy to refine her abilities as an assassin. Rhyas encouraged individuality and took pride in seeing her creation exceed its imagined capabilities but, as Nyxyan’s individuality emerged, began to quietly harbor concern that too much of the old Nixian might yet remain.

name: Name
body:
Rhyas tried to use what little time they had to maximum effect but found herself quickly stretched thin. She was barely able to assist her few shadowmancers and spinners shape flesh and weapons from their resources—each creation robbed her of more energy. Her time overseeing became too divided to offer her brood the attention she wished.
She and Rassyk sparred ceaselessly over the next few days to test their strengths and weaknesses so they could learn to adapt when inevitably faced with Everblight’s servants. They were simultaneously assisting with organizing the scouting and defensive efforts, but those tasks began to become secondary to self-improvement. The rivalry started as adversarial but grew into one of mutual respect and appreciation that they shared a side…and a goal. The manner of their creation ceased to be an active concern as each embraced their role on the cosmic scale, with their impending conflicts seeming a small obstacle to their true purpose, one imparted to them by their mothers.

name: Name
body: Saeryn had placed full confidence in the fate that guided them, but Rhyas—upon appraisal of their purported purpose—failed to be as optimistic. But her doubts regarding her supposed role in the determination of the macrocosm were pushed aside entirely as she hardened herself to face the perpetrator of the destruction of her entire culture. Through her creations, Rhyas had diminished herself beyond the point of vulnerability. Her faith now would have to be placed in those she has built and her ploy with Shyryss. The might of Everblight loomed just beyond her doorstep, even while he cowered in a moldering fortress beyond civilization. In truth, all their refinement meant little against the immensity of the raw power being brought to bear against them. They were but an intricate web of spider silk attempting to withstand a thrown boulder.

name: Name
body: *** Everblight said nothing as Lylyth hastened across the mountainous landscape; still, she sensed his smoldering judgment that pained her almost as much as her own. She knew that pursuing into the mine without more backup was foolish, but she went anyway to please her dragon master, and Fyanna had paid the price. He now gathered most of his warlocks and their forces far from safety to retrieve his three missing athanc shards that could prove vital to his recovery but in doing so left himself with a minimal garrison—his castellan Kryssa and the obsequious Bethayne. Lylyth hadn’t entertained the notion of personal mortality in years yet still experienced Fyanna’s death as if it were her own. All the warlocks felt Everblight’s baleful thoughts as they watched that mechanikal cave-dweller affix Fyanna to the wall and allow Rhyas to claim her prize. Somehow, the two must have struck an unspoken bargain—Everblight was familiar with the cephalyx and their penchant for psychic communication.

name: Name
body: Rhyas was clearly stronger with her sister’s shard; a third would make her most formidable, but she would still be no match for the concentrated rage of Everblight’s Legion. The hills were alive with the Legion’s formations of marching blighted ogrun, led by the ogrun matriarch warlock Anamag, that formed their vanguard while silhouettes of swarming spawn and grotesques flew just above the surface with the warlock Absylonia at their head. Vayl, the great traitor to the Nyss and Everblight’s chief lieutenant, regally perched on a peak that gave vantage to the breadth of the landscape below. She continued to summon the heavy fog that masked their approach from the distant Cygnaran settlements while her Nyss scouts were already filtering into discovered entrances to the tunnels beneath. Vayl had easily risen within the societal ways of the Nyss but was unfulfilled until she had divined Everblight’s coming. She reveled in the destruction of her uncivilized people that she had orchestrated as Everblight’s right hand. She always knew her fate was intertwined with the twins they now sought, but her clairvoyance had become increasingly vague since the Battle of Henge Hold. Soon, their disruption would be settled. The warlocks divided their dragonspawn with Lylyth to replenish her battlegroup as they prepared for the siege that would ultimately end their seditious struggle.

name: Name
body: The magical fog joined the rolling storm clouds that drifted in from the sea. Frequent white flashes with a violet fringe colored the haze as Anamag wound down the mine shaft with an entire army of ogrun warmongers. Known as the Doom Feaster, the former Dhunian priestess Anamag had become cruel and bloodthirsty after becoming blighted. The affliction that gifted her with arcane might also left her with a ceaseless hunger, particularly for the corrupted flesh of her own kind. Her contingent of heavy dragonspawn were likely more than enough to tame whatever was left in the hive as they unleashed endless torrents of dragonfire to precede them, but her ogrun hordes would join for good measure. Ranks of blighted ogrun impatiently shoved and pressed toward the sheer mineshaft, the ogrun raging for fresh meat. Lylyth followed Vayl’s scouting parties with a blighted Nyss army of her own to close in from behind as they began magically flooding the tunnels with cloying acidic mists that would dissolve anything lacking Everblight’s blessings hiding within the deeper regions. They would render the hive system too inhospitable to endure and thus flush Rhyas to her execution.

name: Name
body:
Vayl extended the reach of her magic as she coordinated the forces from afar, and Absylonia roosted like a vulture over her gruesome flock, ready to respond to wherever they were needed. Absylonia had initially been sent to escort Everblight’s favored warlock, Kallus, to his new domain, but she was recalled upon arrival to serve Vayl. She had seen much evolution since she was first blighted. Her newest incarnation as a swift flying terror made her a valuable weapon to launch at any problem, a weapon Vayl was comfortable wielding.
Vayl’s concentration over coordinating the assault was broken by the unnatural cadence to the storm, which despite incessant lightning offered no thunder. Her dragonsight could identify odd shapes in the sky obstructed by the weather. As she reached into the mist with her enhanced senses, the dense blanket of fog peeled away in perfect sheets revealing three large floating weapons platforms. Wild-haired individuals on the bows of the platforms adroitly manipulated rods and levers  that seemed to be creating and directing the storm while purple energy crackled and flashed from the large aft-mounted mechanisms allowing them to defy gravity. No sooner had the airships revealed themselves than the absent thunder was unleashed.

name: Name
body:
The ground quaked and rumbled beneath the broadsides of the airships above. The cascade of cannon-fire joined the barrage from jack-mounted artillery poised beyond the tree lines. The spine-plated carpet of dragon-blighted hosts was swept from the hills near the mine entrance. Humongous chunks of blighted carapace and ruined meat rained down across the landscape as the cannonade found its mark.
Vayl was incensed by the inconvenient timing of these trivialities. She began to reconceal her forces, preparing to magically overpower the efforts of the frail men waving their sticks, and she commanded Absylonia and her swarms to take flight. The sudden patter of dark feathers became a tumult as the smaller blighted beasts were accompanied by a plethora of dragonspawn flapping massive leathery wings. The many shapes lifted as one indiscernible mass of wrath and hunger.
The cannons redirected their fusillade as hundreds of darting shapes took to the skies and a rapid wall of flesh raced toward the three ships. The racking slides of point-defense chain-guns punctuated the air as they swiveled and began to spin. Fiery bursts of bullets hailed into the quickly approaching flock. The air filled with a thick cloud of steaming blighted blood as the creatures were perforated by streams of gunfire. The amassed shrieks split the air, but undeterred, they continued to speed closer. The next fusillade failed to find a mark as the swarm unnaturally reacted as one, a thunderhead of black wings flowing into onrushing spirals through which the shells harmlessly flew.

name: Name
body:
A white-haired woman on the bow of the lead ship twirled her storm rod and created a vortex of wind to hold the ensorcelled fog at bay as Vayl thrust tendrils of freezing mist stretching inward, threatening to blind them from the approaching cloud of teeth and claws. The team of stormsmiths accompanying the woman divided into roles. Some arced flashes of chain lightning that sizzled through the swarm, dancing body to body with piercing blue radiance and causing ashen figures to fall lifelessly after each discharge. Others attempted to assist with the clash of weather dominance.
Klaxons sounded as the airships’ garrison’s boots pounded up to the main decks, formed into units, and fired in volleys at the rushing abominations. They were primarily trained in rapid deployment and ground conflict, so the creatures they faced defied anything they had ever drilled for. The surge of Absylonia’s flock barely thinned as a result of the amassed firepower; the soldiers simply lacked what was necessary to contain the flood. Moments later, their host was upon them.

name: Name
body:
The opening salvo had been devastating, but the might of the Legion was too vast. The hull of the lead ship crunched and boomed as talons raked it and thick bodies smashed into it. Chain-guns began to whirl and fire wildly as probing beaks of blighted vultures hunted the gunners’ eyes over the mantlets, pecking clean through their goggles. Living gargoyles called grotesques became impaled on hastily applied bayonets as the firing squads found themselves overwhelmed. Flying serpents swept across the decks, impaling any unfortunate enough to be in their reach, while others sprayed dragonfire into the openings of the cannon deck. With the lead ship engulfed and completely coated by gnashing and feasting spawn, the warcaster captain consolidated his forces to make a final stand.
The airship on the port flank exploded as its powder stores met the inescapable blaze of an enormous dragonspawn called an archangel that burned through the hull with a continuous stream of superheated breath. Absylonia gutted the captain of the ship on the starboard flank while her forces breached the ship and engaged the cannoneers in melee combat. Vayl, seeing the battle in the sky resolving quickly, redirected her efforts to smothering the ground forces with impenetrable haze. She could see Absylonia’s eyes gleam with hunger as they looked toward the remaining captain and took flight. The man of about thirty stood boldly in his pristine armor, defiantly awaiting his fate. Absylonia’s long, slender tail whipped behind her in anticipation as she streaked toward him.

name: Name
body: The firing line established by the Cygnarans in the woods, with ’jacks providing fire support, was well organized and blistering to approach, but when the stampede of heavy dragonspawn and blighted ogrun reached them, the Cygnarans folded beneath the considerable might and numbers of the enemy. Flares signaling retreat were consumed by the magical gloom occluding everything as the Legion unimpeded by the darkness thanks to their draconic sight, swept forward. The retreat became a route as dread overcame the human lines. A shockwave knocked trees and shook the ground as a blazing airship crashed through the old growth, igniting the surrounding forest. Ash and dust began to fall across the battlefield as the Legion marched on.

name: Name
body:
***
Rhyas had attempted to establish a dynamic and responsive defense to hit and fade, knowing a stand-up fight would be futile, but corrosive gas had consumed many of the connecting tunnels that would allow such maneuverability. Quickfang scouts reported echoes of loud blasts above, leading her to wonder if they were attempting to seal the exits. The scouts also reported corridors being flooded with fire as the Legion’s vanguard probed deeper and closer. She decided they could not sit idle and wait to be surrounded; instead, she had her spawn create targeted cave-ins to protect the cathedral and marched toward Anamag and her blazing host, Rassyk eagerly in the lead.
***
As Anamag observed the licking flames from a carnivean’s gout subside, framed in the orange glow came an ogrun-sized, singed draconic humanoid that lunged forward, sinking a massive blade into the carnivean’s thick armored hide. He then fluidly sidestepped and brought the massive sword down parallel to its shoulders, decapitating the draconic hulk leading the way. Although unprepared for the ambush and caught off-guard by the new assailant, Anamag’s only thought was that she hoped it had a heart, for she would take great pleasure in eating it.

name: Name
body:
***
The white-haired woman unleashed a final surge of lightning that burst in a bright nimbus as it hissed and fried a hemisphere of grotesques before she was wrenched in half by Absylonia, her lifeless fingertips crackling with fading latent energy as her torso slid across the blood-slicked deck. A warjack unleashed both spinning arm-mounted barrels upon her, despite her shifting some of the damage, the many bullets succeeded at shredding one wing before she managed to guide small dragonspawn into its path, mindlessly taking the rest of the shots meant for her. A handful of surviving soldiers slipped and crawled to form up on the captain, ducking beneath the fire of his warjack battlegroup as Absylonia’s darting and streaking forces closed in. A hammer-headed dragonspawn smashed into the firing ’jack, beating it back with successive bashes until it tipped over the edge and its heavy frame plummeted out of sight. Another warjack armed with a long-barreled cannon and a giant hammer crushed the spawn’s armored head, splitting it and sending fragments of chitin ricocheting off its steel frame. When the captain went to enhance the ’jack’s onslaught in order to finish it, Absylonia was already upon him.

name: Name
body: A flurry of slashes pierced his power field and raked his armor. Although his saber was ceremonial and looked to be of little use on an airship, it turned out that it was not mere decoration. The captain skillfully countered some of her strikes and opened a grisly streak across her chest with the edge of his saber. Enraged by the wound, Absylonia maneuvered him toward the edge with feints and then bum-rushed him overboard. His sword exited her back as he buried it through her stomach when she crashed into him, and he gripped her wing with his other hand, pinning them together. He tried to twist the blade, but her flesh was too thick and resilient. In a savage embrace, the two plunged down into the murk. With air whistling across his mangled armor, the captain tried to hold onto her for both revenge and spite as they tumbled, but she placed her clawed foot upon his face, gripped it tightly, and bodily kicked them apart. She clumsily attempted to maintain flight with her shredded wing as the captain vanished in the haze.

name: Name
body: *** Vayl assured Everblight that the setback was inevitable, given their brazen level of activity so close to civilization, but it would do nothing to compromise their victory. A second explosion thundered as another airship erupted as it crashed to the ground. The shockwave of dust washed over her as she stood unfazed, but then a new sound tolled. The sky tore open. Vertigo overtook her; her ears bled as her body shook. She felt as if she might vibrate apart. The clouds began to disperse as control slipped from her, and the roar that reverberated across the battlefield cracked stone and uprooted foliage as combatants on both sides were knocked to the ground. Hurricane force winds began to rip across the mountainscape. Vegetation steamed, bubbled, and dissolved as a vast dark shape descended upon them. *** The hive rumbled, dust and rocks filled the air, and rats skittered in packs through the darkness, all heralding the arrival above. Rhyas smiled – Shyryss had been successful in her mission. Rhyas was able to detect the locations of all Everblight’s athanc shards. This would be extremely valuable to her if she were on the hunt, but the talent would be useless upon death. The ability to locate these shards, however, would be very valuable to Everblight’s foes. During a clash between the Dragon Alliance and Toruk, Rhyas and Saeryn had previously bargained for the great dragon Blighterghast to leave the Legion be, which he contemptuously accepted in the moment out of necessity. Releasing Blighterghast from that vow would do nothing to stop him from consuming Shyryss or the rest of the Khymaera on sight, but a promise of continued information on the whereabouts of Everblight’s shards? Well, how could he resist such an offer?

name: Name
body: *** Anamag blasted Rassyk with a hex that dispelled his offensive enhancements, began to magically guide her forces’ attacks, and unleashed her dragonspawn upon him all at once. The second carnivean did much to make up for the slain first one. It battered and bit deep into Rassyk’s metallic flesh, forcing him to redirect damage through his bonded connection to a three-headed Hydrix, opening jagged bite marks on its serpentine hide. The carnivean’s chitinous plates thickened; it sprouted additional bony spines as it readied itself for retaliation. Streams of dragonfire washed over Rassyk, but despite his armor beginning to glow white hot, the draconic origins of his creation left him mostly unscathed. The tunnel was too tight for a full confrontation, allowing Anamag to slide safely behind her forces as they pressed to join in. Still, a question nagged at her. Could this be what Rhyas had become, or was this something new, a cephalyx creation perhaps? Her target broke free and pulled his beasts to his flanks defensively as he counterattacked against the carnivean. This one did not go down as easily as the last, but his Hydrix managed to latch its lamprey-like central head onto its unprotected belly and gnawed a hole to its vitals, turning the carnivean into a roadblock in the already cramped arena. The engagement became bogged down as both forces tried to navigate the accumulating bodies in the narrow passages.

name: Name
body:
***
Blighterghast’s immense jaws snatched the mockery of draconic majesty, the archangel, from the sky, compressing it to pulp. He let its lifeless enormity fall from his mouth as he released a deluge of steaming bile that blanketed the hosts in the tree line, dissolving all nearby forces into a viscous stew that washed across the uneven ground, settling in fetid pools. He landed heavily on the bulk of the remaining spawn with a shockwave that could be felt for miles. With the visible army mostly rendered toothless, he sought his prize. His eyes were affixed to the regal sorceress on the mountainside, but undulating flutters of an injured warlock attempting to fly away drew his gaze away. The maimed warlock summoned her bevy of spawn to intervene, but the remaining swarm was but a cloud of gnats attempting to obstruct a meteor. With a violent tempest that cleansed the land, Blighterghast again took flight and flew through the swarm undeterred until his mouth closed around Absylonia.  An apology to Everblight escaped her lips as she was consumed by the greatest of Toruk’s brood.

name: Name
body:
***
Nyxyan slipped with her strike team to the hidden flank of Anamag’s spearhead. She gathered her Quickfangs in their secretive tunnel and prepared for an opening. If Rassyk could force Anamag back or force her to engage, she’d be helpless against Nyxyan’s smothering darkness. Seemingly limitless blighted ogrun continued to pour into the tunnels, passing just before her as they began to fill every corridor in search of new avenues of attack. If nothing stemmed the tide, they could lose the chance at Anamag’s life, but wait too long and they might lose their chance to escape. Rhyas would be in position soon.
She sensed the movements through the walls of the caverns. She traced Rhyas’ actions as she engaged.
Choosing a choke point to stifle the ceaseless advance of Everblight’s armies, Rhyas pinched off reinforcements and began driving her forces from behind Anamag. A Hydrix crafted as a roadblock sealed the entrance with its armor-plated heads as they beat back the pressing ogrun through the slender gap. Rhyas carved her way with shock troops of her own as her Death Dealers went toe-to toe with Everblight’s ogrun. They were made as more easily replicable versions of Rassyk, lacking his sorcerous inclinations or extra imbued power. The commotion was Nyxyan’s cue to engage.

name: Name
body:
She bent the light around her Vypex, turning it into a living shadow, and launched it at the hideous ogrun warlock. It immaterially slithered through the obstructing wall and the ogrun’s bodyguards and manifested on the other side as it brought its two cleaving arm blades down into her putrid bulk. She shrieked in unison with her Scythean as she redirected the wound, crippling her beast. Anamag shook off the confusion and hungered at the appearance of the new enemy, as it could empower her dark rituals. Her ogrun warmongers buried their heavy blades in the worm, slaying it outright, as Anamag drew upon its escaping life essence to further bolster her forces.
Nyxyan had hoped for a fast resolution—she was not suited for prolonged engagement, but she still had more tricks up her sleeve. She rolled aside the camouflaged exit and launched out with a whirling burst of darkness that gripped and bound those it contacted. Quickfang stalkers, human-sized Khymaera designed to adopt Rhyas’ ways of the assassin, leapt upon the bodyguards. As some buried their blades into the off-guard ogrun, others acrobatically cleared their lines and tore into the bloated caster. Her Scythean grew deep tears from transferred wounds until it could take no more. Anamag’s blood spilled black as she was opened with well-placed strokes, but she managed to unsteadily stay on her feet. As she focused on her own survival, her protective forces began to falter all around her.

name: Name
body:
Berserking warmongers cleared Nyxyan’s stalkers away from Anamag with brutal sweeping strokes and tried to make a tight wall as Rassyk broke through her vanguard. Anamag began to retreat but could see Rhyas slicing her way through the forces behind. Hundreds of ogrun raced through the maze of tunnels to support, but none were where they were needed. Everblight’s wrath guided Anamag to expend all her forces to return his wayward shards. She unleashed a tribal war cry as a call to carnage. The weapons of her forces paradoxically glowed black as an aura of undiluted death emanated from each tip and they redirected everything toward Rhyas.
***
The Death Dealers lived up to their namesake but succumbed to the punishing charge of Anamag’s last stand. As Rhyas’ personal retinue fell and the bite of dark blades interfered with her ability to heal herself, she knew it was kill or be killed. She tried to find a path through the wall of meat that protected her target, but Anamag was staying tight to her guards to stymie further assassins. Anamag’s face was gashed and twisted in anger as she compelled her troops forward to salvage a victory from this massive folly. Rhyas had felt Lylyth mired within the labyrinth, but she must’ve found a pass, as her shard now sped closer toward her flank. As Rhyas tried to decide upon the most prudent course of action while being so close to her target, she suddenly sensed above that the decision was made for her.

name: Name
body: "To the cathedral!" she shouted as she dashed away from combat and raced to outrun the inevitable. *** The forces of the Legion scattered like roaches exposed to light—caught in this trap unawares and positioned as they were, they lacked the concentrated power to oppose an entity the magnitude of Blighterghast. The queenly Nyss warlock whom Blighterghast had his sights set on had vanished while he consumed the flying one, but he was told their plan. The ambassador of the twin traitors informed him that the Legion had come for his athanc and planned to approach him unseen utilizing a tunnel system within a mine. Cave-ins and rockslides resounded continuously as he landed near the now barren focal point of the converging blighted troops. Fallen trees and bodies drew toward him from a sudden squall as he braced his gargantuan form against the excavation site and deeply inhaled. His claws crushed and expanded the entrance, and he stared directly down the shaft where he could see myriad abominations hurriedly descending into the depths. Placing his mouth just above the carved mine shaft, he forcefully exhaled. With tidal force, a scalding geyser of reeking naphtha was injected into the pit.

name: Name
body: A burst of displaced air blew out eardrums and sent the spelunking forces tumbling against hard stone, crushing armor and shattering bones. Everblight warned his warlocks through shared sight of what was coming, but there was nowhere to go. A piercing whistle preceded the cascade of caustic breath as it flushed the forces within the mine. The consumptive fluid devoured all it touched, liquefying the mighty hordes into a steaming residue. Rhyas had sensed the massive shape of Blighterghast approach with only moments to spare. She knew manipulating a power of his enormity would not be without consequence. *** Roughly half of their forces eventually met back at the cathedral, including Rassyk and Nyxyan. It would be days before they’d know whether Shyryss was spared or not, but they held on to a slim hope. Rhyas mourned her forces that would not be able to be remade as well as all the potential forces whose materials were obliterated. This setback was significant, but the host of cephalyx was still mostly fresh and ready. She felt Lylyth’s athanc speed away through the tunnels with the scattered ogrun, Vayl’s raced even farther, but Absylonia’s was undetectable.

name: Name
body:
Once all signs of Blighterghast’s presence had faded, they made their move. Winding their way back amidst a sputtering slurry of what presumably had once been the great ogrun chieftain’s horde, they saw what remained of the mighty draconic servant. A steaming and shapeless form clung to life using every ounce of imbued power to stay alive. Anamag’s dissolving flesh left her hairless, smooth, and nearly unrecognizable save for the gifted power emanating from her. She dragged her torso across the acrid ground with her remaining arm, leaving a stained trail of blood and ichor that oozed from where her legs had once extended, marbling the sludge behind her. A Hydrix, customized for resistance to corrosives, wriggled through the muck and retrieved her fading remains coiled within its tail.
Rhyas stared into the fuming cavities that had once housed the shared eyes of the voyeuristic master she served. "You shouldn’t have come for us. You haven’t even caught a glimpse of what we’re capable of, but don’t worry. In time you will."

name: Name
body: With a blur of movement, Anamag’s head seemed to melt off her neck from a fresh wound, even though Rhyas’ blade was already resheathed. Rhyas had no interest in preserving any trace of Anamag’s repulsiveness. As the only of Everblight’s warlocks to bear no shard, she was left to fade with her cursed legacy in the darkness. *** Saeryn was now nearly in full control of her half of the joined shards. She had already been plotting to test her own hands at the fabrication she witnessed through her sister, distracting herself with the near limitless powers of creation that laid before her. With the cephalyx at bay, the Legion decimated, and their own power rising, they were approaching the turning point in their ascension. They would no longer be on their heels; they would be on the hunt. Strategically, Everblight had to fall, but the reckoning in store for the treacherous Nyss that sold out their civilization would be even sweeter. When we’re ready, she promised herself, we will find Vayl.

name: Name
body: Meanwhile… The frozen body of a Cygnaran soldier was shattered by one of Vayl’s surviving spawn. Red fragments sealed with hoarfrost cascaded across the ground, slick from Vayl’s cold arcane wrath. Entering Cygnar under the veil of magical concealment and through a path of Everblight’s secretive machinations was fairly simple; exiting past fortified and vigilant troops was proving near impossible. The longer they idled, the more soldiers responded to their presence, and they were no longer in a position of power. Lylyth was securing a route through the wilderness while Vayl followed. Ceaseless gunfire hounded them as her spawn stayed close to shield her. Her eyes never left the horizon as she repeatedly scanned for any signs of Blighterghast’s insatiable hunger. The regality and poise normally inextricable from Vayl’s countenance had vanished. Her pure white robes were stained and tattered as she fled across the frontier. She was more aware of her degraded appearance than any others.

name: Name
body:
"I have failed you, but I will return to you. In time, I shall show them what it means to cross your Right Hand." She said this to Everblight through their bond with her cool confidence, despite the pangs of uncertainty that clawed at her. Her usual clairvoyance that she divined from her crafted oraculi had been inexplicably blocked, leaving her equally in the dark as others.
"No." Everblight’s response to her rhetoric was simple yet surprising, and it hung in the air with vast uncertainty of implication.
"We... shall not seek vengeance?" Vayl could not deduce the meaning in such an enigmatic declaration.
"You are no longer my Right Hand. In light of your deeds, I have a greater purpose in mind for you."
Her years of servitude and devotion on the brink of being rewarded, Vayl straightened with pride as she dared to ask. "I am ever your humble servant. What purpose, my master?"
"Bait."
